newsitem.title: MEXICO: Some Mexican truckers not eager to enter U.S.
newsitem.headline: Some Mexican truckers not eager to enter U.S.

text.p: Mexican truck drivers associated with the National Cargo Transport Chamber are not eager to enter the United States, as stipulated in the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the organization said on Wednesday.

U.S. authorities and transportation analysts have said the border could be opened to Mexican trucks by the end of the month after a delay of more than two years and bilateral legal battles. Mexican trucks have been blocked from entering the United States amid charges that the vehicles failed to conform to U.S. standards.

"We are not interested in entering the United States. The longer it takes to open the border, the better, because it gives us more time to prepare ourselves," the chamber's president, Bernardo Lijtszain, told reporters.

"I am sure that many people think differently than we do, such as the tomato and avocado growers and steelmakers, who need to sell their products in the exterior," he said. The chamber does not represent all Mexican truck drivers.
Mexico formally protested the U.S. delay in allowing Mexican trucks to cross the border through a bilateral NAFTA commission. A ruling on the complaint is expected by the end of February.
Still, Lijtszain said the chamber preferred a closed border, with "neither (Mexican truckers) entering the United States, nor them coming here."
"If there is a modification of NAFTA, we will probably ask that cargo truckers be excluded," he said.
Lijtszain said Mexican truckers were not prepared to compete with their U.S. counterparts.
"Technically we could be equal in infrastructure. The only problem is that the Mexican economy can still not pay what is required to be in conditions to equally compete with the Americans," he added.
U.S. labor unions have opposed the opening of the border to Mexican trucks, saying cheaper Mexican labor was a threat to U.S. jobs.
